purpose: Specialist reference outcomes for testing wearable-derived ANS features; these tests are NOT wrist sensors
measurement_vs_reference_rule: Wearable feature predictors must be generated without using any specialist outcome, reference result or later visit data
clinical_status: No same-person reference-linked participants acquired; no diagnostic accuracy estimates

references.watch_surrogate_analyses: Test coupling of standardized wearable HR/vascular responses with invasively recorded MSNA during matched posture or provocation; no direct sympathetic nerve readout from wrist
confounding_and_limits: microneurography is invasive and technically specialized
resting MSNA varies greatly across individuals
MSNA outflow to muscle does not equal sudomotor or global ANS function

references.modality: 123I-MIBG scintigraphy or relevant cardiac sympathetic PET
references.watch_surrogate_analyses: Compare blinded wearable cardiac autonomic features against imaging assessments in selected clinical populations
confounding_and_limits: radiotracer imaging
myocardial disease/diabetes/medications may alter tracer uptake
not a general ANS disease label

references.display_name: Skin small-fibre and sweat-gland nerve morphology
references.modality: skin biopsy with IENFD and separately measured sweat-gland nerve-fibre density
references.domain: somatic and peripheral autonomic small fibres, depending on fibre type and site
references.watch_surrogate_analyses: Test whether wearable functional abnormalities track independently characterized sweat-gland innervation; distinguish from general IENFD
confounding_and_limits: IENFD alone is primarily a somatic small-fibre measure
biopsy site and laboratory norms matter
structural findings need clinical and physiological correlation

references.display_name: Corneal nerve fibre length, density and branching
references.watch_surrogate_analyses: Exploratory correlation against independently confirmed neuropathy status; not a specific ANS label
confounding_and_limits: corneal nerve measures are not ANS-specific
sensitivity and specificity depend on comparator and disease setting
corneal disease and imaging methodology may matter

references.domain: selected synucleinopathies, e.g. pure autonomic failure, Parkinson disease, MSA or DLB
references.watch_surrogate_analyses: Separate predefined disease-specific analysis only; never substitute positivity for generalized ANS dysfunction
confounding_and_limits: does not detect all causes of autonomic dysfunction
study-population spectrum and expert diagnosis affect generalizability
pathology positivity and autonomic severity are different endpoints

references.modality: gastric emptying studies; motility/transit tests; manometry
references.watch_surrogate_analyses: Evaluate whether future changes in wearable metrics predict independently verified GI motility impairment in an appropriate clinical cohort
confounding_and_limits: motility is affected by enteric, muscular, pharmacological and structural factors
symptoms alone are not objective autonomic outcomes
method and segment of GI tract must be specified

references.modality: urodynamic testing and postvoid residual assessments
references.watch_surrogate_analyses: Compare wearable metrics with blinded neurological/urological assessment in a defined disorder
confounding_and_limits: obstruction, medication, pelvic floor and other non-neural causes
urodynamic abnormalities alone do not prove autonomic nerve damage
phenotype and sex/anatomy affect interpretation

references.modality: Schirmer or other standardized tear and salivary secretion tests
references.watch_surrogate_analyses: Use only as supportive organ-specific outcome with documented competing causes
confounding_and_limits: dry eye, gland disease, dehydration and medications
secretion also depends on ocular and gland local factors
not a stand-alone generalized ANS dysfunction label

design_rules: Define a separate diagnosis/phenotype and timepoint for each reference target.
Keep reference results and specialist modalities excluded from wearable-only predictor features.
Use independent expert diagnosis or distinct future outcome to prevent circular CASS/test component labels.
Group all longitudinal records of a participant in a single validation fold; use external cohort for replication.
Compare PPG-only, multimodal wearable, and clinical-context baselines on matched participants; estimate uncertainty and calibration.
Treat absent specialist measurements as missing, not normal; do not require all eight tests on every patient.
Do not claim clinical accuracy unless appropriate real participants with matched wearable and independently adjudicated clinical references exist.
